partnershipPlan: Two bereaved family members and a palliative care volunteer review the family letter and questionnaire; a ward nurse and a resident review the prompt wording.
socialListening: No social media listening; the hospital's bereavement service feedback is read in anonymised form.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The first time anyone asked what Dad wanted was the night before he died.
items.implication: Measure timing of the first documented conversation.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If the prompt only wants a code status, that is all we will write.
items.implication: Rate note content, not only whether a note exists.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I would rather be asked what matters to me than told what the options are.
items.implication: Include patient values and priorities in the quality score.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Another alert on a busy ward just gets clicked away.
items.implication: Measure staff time and prompt dismissal as balancing measures.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: A letter three months later is fine, but a phone call would have been too soon.
items.implication: Let families choose the route and timing of contact.

summary: Five composite voices on timing, tick boxes, what matters, workload and family contact.
